newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE wants Serbia opposition win fully recognised.
newsitem.headline: OSCE wants Serbia opposition win fully recognised.

text.p: Europe's top security body on Thursday called for full recognition by Serbia of the opposition's victory in municipal polls held on November 17.

"Step-by-step concessions to opposition on what ought to be a merely mechanical issue - translating the results into seats - is simply not the way to handle this situation," said Niels Helveg Petersen, Foreign Minister of Denmark and chairman-in-office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation (OSCE).

The Vienna-based OSCE two weeks ago backed a report by former Spanish premier Felipe Gonzalez on the disputed local poll in Serbia and called on Belgrade for prompt implementation of its recommendations.
Petersen, addressing the OSCE's permanent council, said Belgrade had not complied fast enough but that the body remained open for dialogue.
"Our door is wide open. But the FRY (Federal Republic of Yugoslavia) does not seem to want to walk through it," he said.

Petersen added that without democratisation there was no chance to resolve the crisis in Serbia, which has seen almost two months of mass protests against the annulment of opposition victories by the government of President Slobodan Milosevic.
